Oh my...

I've felt like writing a review on this for a little while, and as I firstly acknowledge that this isn't any where near a relevant date based on it's release - I have completed Fallout 4 so at the very least I have a more rounded opinion that someone who wrote a review based on less than 2 hours game time.

I could give you a huge list, but I'll keep it simple.

Ultimately you'll come away feeling disappointed - there is NO depth to anything.

Where is bob the tree?
Where's the republic of Dave?
Where are you Gary's?

I of course am speaking figuritively rather than literally - the point I'm making is that there are NO memorable side quests, nothing even remotely slightly entertaining which fallout 3 had in abundance.

Even the original FO3 ending, which DEEPLY annoyed the community - is better than the ending we get in Fallout 4.

Everything is pretty much wrapped around the main storyline which ultimately leads you down a road that makes you feel it's all pretty linear and you were (no pun intended) Railroaded into the ending.

On a positive note, I think that Bethesda has tried to make 'good guys/bad guys' far more ambigous in this game, this is a case to be made for and against pretty much all factions, but despite all this, it still ends us with 2 basic end choices both of which will make you feel deeply unfulfilled.

Another classic Fallout game. Ignore all the negative hate and get it.

More of an evolution versus revolution over Fallout 3, it adds crafting and settlement management mechanics that at least for me were somewhat unwelcome additions (following certain factions limits the need for doing this, fortunately).  The same themes of family and duty are present here, as well as the often weighty side narratives.  There are great additions to graphics fidelity (at the expense of performance like most newer titles), and there are a lot of re-used assets from Fallout 3.  That said, Massachusetts is a great location, maybe even better than DC with its densely packed urban landscapes and contrasting pastoral outlying areas.  While many will find the options to side with different factions (several of which have dark sides, and none of which are entirely "bad" either) a plus, I found the more straightforward narrative of FO3 (with the Broken Steel DLC anyway) to be overall more satisfying.  There are gaps in the plot (and hackneyed resolutions/solutions).  The main story left me wanting.  I found resources (esp. caps, certain materials and ammo types) to be too scarce for my liking, especially near the main endgame.  After all, this is not technically a survival game.  7/10  Recommended if you're a fan of Fallout's world and premise, but aren't looking for the best narrative.

Played on i5 3570, 16Gb RAM, R9 380 4Gb.  I experienced a handful of AMD driver crashes.  Clean (using DDU) re-installation of latest drivers along with verifying game cache and running in full-screen window borderless mode drastically reduced and nearly eliminated such crashes.  Experienced 50-60fps on Ultra in most areas, dense urban areas or indoor areas with lots of shadowing caused drops as low as 30fps.  Changing overall setting to Medium resulted in more consistent 60fps with drops in aforementioned areas as low as ~40fps.

I have a really long review,, but for some reason the steamclient wont let me post it.

All I have to say for now is:

Instead of being "TES: Wasteland Edition" like the previous games, (although I did like New Vegas - it actually felt like Fallout through the lens of the TES engine) Fallout 4 is "TES:Fallout - zombie edition". I do NOT play Fallout so I can be in the Walking Dead. However, that appears to be what this game is.

Walk into a ruined town, get mobbed by 20 feral ghouls. See a cabin, approach slowly. Get mobbed by 5 feral ghouls. Walk into a railroad station, get mobbed by 10 feral ghouls. Walk into a building, guess what! Feral ghouls.

And when I saw mobbed, I mean it. These are "running zombie" fast. Hell, more like "teleport zombie" fast. They arent so bad if theres a few, but its a giant pain when you've got 20 zipping at you.

I'm sick of f'n feral ghouls. They are EVERYWHERE in this game. I like the new creepy feral ghoul models, but I guess Beth REALLY liked the new feral ghoul model because they stuck feral ghouls all over the f'n place. Hell, I open up a toolbox, it wouldnt surprise me one bit if a feral ghoul popped out.

There really isnt much else. No sense of a cohesive rebuilding society on the brink of war that you got in New Vegas.
 So far its just emptyness, abandoned buildings, and feral ghouls all over the f'n place...with the random raider group/base or wasteland monster to round things out.

I was hoping with New Vegas, (the only one of the new games whos story setting and writing felt like "real" Fallout) Beth finally understood what made the Fallout series great...but I guess not. 

I can give you a hint though, it WASN'T feral ghouls.

Feral ghouls.

Fallout 4 is a difficult game to review.  I'll do my best to try and make this review post concise. Try, I said. 

    What I enjoy about Fallout 4 is that the open-world you're thrown into allows you to progress in a unique manner separate from anyone else's experiences. Do I want to do nothing but build settlements and screw the main quest? Sure, I could do that. Do I want to go around exploring every nook and cranny? Sure, I could do that too.  How about raid a barracks held by Gunners with nothing but my baseball bat? Yep, can do that too. Which reminds me, the combat is fluid and enjoyable as well (for some period of time, but even combat looses it's luster after a while). 

     Now, don't get me wrong. The aformentioned reasons can be justification enough to get some good playing hours out of Fallout. Yet, oddly enough, the game looses it's appeal very quickly. There's a lot to do, but none of it feels in depth. The story elements and quests in the game are not fleshed out.  For example, I recall when I first discovered Combat Zone, I thought to myself "Oh man, this is awesome. I get to do some cage fighting". Well guess again.  It turned out to be just another slaughter of pathetic raiders. Who by the way pose no challenge in regards to combat difficulty, even on survival mode.  In fact, if you delve into the scripts/voice clips of the game, you'll see that Bethesda apparently had plans to allow for cage fighting and flesh out the story. I guess those plans went out the door because they wanted to release it by November. 

     As for the workshop, that becomes monotonous. I mean, what's the point of building a settlement? Just for the hell of it? Or are you doing it only because Preston tells you do so? It just becomes superfluous. 

   Now, my biggest gripe here are the bugs in this game.  In a open-world "rpg" (can we even call it that? More like a straight up FPS) setting, immersion is key in making that world believable, but I can't mention enough how often the bugs in this game break that immersion. Oh that's weird...I killed that raider but he's still doing the Michael Jackson moonwalk.  Did that Brahma just fall out of the sky?  I swear Dogmeat was just following me? Now he's dissapeared? Wait, that Legendary Deathclaw is stuck because a tree trunk is in his way.  Well, let's just wait here for several minutes and see if his AI can figure a way around that tree trunk...nope, guess not. Well that's easy, just gonna gun him down where he stands. Oh, and by the way, I consider the AI a buggy part of Fallout.  Stupidity is a word I cannot express enough of the AI system. This is primarily because the pathing system is just horrendous. Your followers, dumb. The enemies, dumb. Dogmeat, dumb.  Not to mention, this pathing system unfortunately includes you. I'm going to access this computer here and...oh wait, what's going on? Why am I walking endlessly towards the computer in first person view?  Why am I not progressing forward?! For Fuck's sake! Damn, no good piece of *&%$ small ass tin can that's on the ground preventing me from accessing said computer! 

    So finally, to sum it all up, what do I think of Fallout 4? It reminds me of a sleazy car dealership trying to sell a crap car. Looks shiny on the outside, promises lots of features, but when you get down to the nitty gritty, it's junk.  None of it is in depth, none of it is fleshed out (save for the combat perhaps) and the actions or dialogue choices you make don't make a damn difference in this post-apocalyptic world.  And here's the kicker.  People will still justify and praise to god almighty why it's ok for this game to be in such a beta state.   Last I checked, each individual did not pay $60 (unless you got it on discount) to the modders to improve upon Bethesda's game. And yet here we are, as usual. Another buggy release made by Bethesda, based on an old outdated engine no less. Look at the comments, the reviews (the positive ones even)...Bethesda releases have been synonymous with "buggy" games.  There are those who acknowledge this as if it's ok.  As if somehow, Bethesda is exempt from harsh criticism for releasing another unoptimized, unfinished game.  There will always be those who justify why buying that crap car is a good idea just like how there are those who will justify Bethesda's release of buggy, unfinished games.

I did enjoy hooking up with my girlfriend and getting a nice lesbian relationship going.  I wish we could have gotten nekkid at bedtime.  I guess you can't have everything.

This is a disappointing Fallout game. If you read many of the reviews on here, you will see exactly why it is. As a Fallout RPG, it lacks so much that made the previous games so memorable, such as unique character customization (stats and skill-wise. The actual character creation in this game is pretty amazing) and multiple dialouge options. I also found a lack of noteable side quests in this game, something that F3 and NV had in spades. HOWEVER, Fallout 4 is still an amazing experience that is definitely worth your money. Compared to its predecessors, Fallout 4 takes 2 steps forwards and 1 step back. It improves on so much, such as the combat and the world, but, as stated before, it forgets to include what made the previous games great. There is still a lot to explore and see in this game, and you will have a blast. It is just a very disappointing game, and I feel that disappointment makes the experience worse. I still had fun, though.

Do you like skyrim? Do you like fallout 3 or any other rpg games? If you do I do not recommend this, I will explain that a bit later.

But if you like a casual open world shooter, like metal gear solid or grand theft auto, then this might be for you.

Now, personally I am disappointed in how this game turned out. But I guess I am just one of those old nostalgic players that call it "dumbed down". But if I had to give you any proof of this to be true, I would point right at the dialogue and questing systems.

Skyrim had roughly 90 quests all in all, how many does fallout 4 have? Around 40. How many options did the player have to react in conversation in skyrim? Varied but usually around 6+, which were on no way cut and paste options like fallout 4: Yes, No, Sarcasm, Question. I wish i loved this game, i bought the anthology edition during the hype and i had already played 3 and new vegas on xbox for around 500 hours each, both of which i loved. And boy, if i could show you the hours i had on skyrim on my xbox...at least 1500 probably more. The point of me stating those is to say that i loved bethesda games...but if you loved the old Bethesda games I don't think you will enjoy yourself too long after the main mission in fallout 4.

Gunplay has improved, and weapon and armor customization are pretty good, but that's about it for improvements, which just solidifies the fact that they focused on the gunplay more than the rpg elements

Cons are quests, dialogue, relationships with other npcs, settlement mode being nothing more than a shallow tacked on element that won't be much more than a nuisance end game, and the presence of voiced protagonists that limit player creativity.
